title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.24017v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The emerging W3C WebMCP proposal enables LLM agents to invoke tools exposed by web pages. In multi-party web environments, however, integrating agent execution into a browser security model centered on the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) leaves insufficient provenance and lifecycle guarantees for agent-accessible tools, creating three risks: subject-attribution spoofing, uncontrolled tool lifecycles, and semantic prompt injection. We propose WebMCP-Phalanx, a dual-layer agent runtime architecture. Its first layer provides a browser-native trust anchor that binds each tool to its registering principal through cryptographically protected capability credentials and propagates provenance labels throughout the tool lifecycle. Its second layer separates semantic inspection from privileged tool use. A Quarantine Agent (Q-LLM), without tool invocation authority, inspects tool metadata, outputs, and page-supplied content for prompt injection. Validate

translated_title: WebMCP-Phalanx：为浏览器集成LLM代理强制和刻画信任边界
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24017v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：新兴的W3C WebMCP提案使LLM代理能够调用网页暴露的工具。然而，在多参与方网络环境中，将代理执行集成到以同源策略（SOP）为中心的浏览器安全模型中，无法为代理可访问的工具提供充分的来源和生命周期保证，从而产生三个风险：主体归属欺骗、不受控制的工具生命周期和语义提示注入。我们提出WebMCP-Phalanx，一种双层代理运行时架构。其第一层提供浏览器原生的信任锚点，通过加密保护的能力凭证将每个工具绑定到其注册主体，并在整个工具生命周期中传播来源标签。其第二层将语义检查与特权工具使用分离。一个隔离代理（Q-LLM），在没有工具调用权限的情况下，检查工具元数据、输出和页面提供的内容以检测提示注入。
tldr: 本文提出WebMCP-Phalanx，一种双层代理运行时架构，通过浏览器原生信任锚点和隔离代理检查，解决浏览器集成LLM代理中的信任边界问题，防止主体欺骗、生命周期失控和提示注入。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes WebMCP-Phalanx, a dual-layer agent runtime architecture that enforces trust boundaries for browser-integrated LLM agents via a browser-native trust anchor and a quarantine agent, mitigating subject spoofing, lifecycle control, and prompt injection risks.
